summary.text:
The task is to judge whether the exact BOOK ENTRY is the best explanation of the supplied scriptural evidence for the term "Life (the life)".
{
  "verdict": "PERSUADED",
  "core_identification": "Covenant existence — the life lived walking in the Way according to God's law",
  "strongest_counter": "Eternal divine life (zōē) given by God through Christ, with Christ himself as the embodiment and source of that life",
  "comparison": "The supplied texts and chapter supply a tighter, more integrated reading than the common interpretation. Deuteronomy 30:19-20 and Leviticus 18:5 explicitly frame 'life' as covenant blessing produced by obedience to the law ('choose life', 'he is thy life if you keep my statutes'). Matthew 7:14 links the narrow way (Torah-shaped conduct) directly to life. John 14:6 is not left as a standalone christological title but is unpacked in the chapter as the three titles (way, truth, life) converging on covenant existence: the way is covenant-conduct, the truth is the law itself, and the life is the existence that flows from walking it. This single symbolic framework accounts for every cited verse without contradiction or special pleading. The common reading, while dominant in Johannine scholarship, treats the OT covenantal texts as secondary or separate registers and must posit a shift in emphasis when moving from Deuteronomy to John 14:6. The book's derivation from the Law and Prophets (via the parable method) explains the full set of references with fewer unsupported steps and greater textual continuity.

support_scope.description: Support for the exact glossary BOOK ENTRY only, never for the supporting chapter as a whole.

book_secondary_elaborations.description: Secondary assertions actually printed in the glossary BOOK ENTRY; exclude chapter-only claims.

unsupported_glossary_assertions.description: Material assertions actually printed in the BOOK ENTRY that the evidence does not support. Must be empty for FULL and nonempty for CORE_ONLY.

chapter_only_objections.description: Objections to applications or arguments found only in the supporting chapter. Preserved for later chapter review and excluded from the glossary scope ruling.

instructions: Return only the requested structured result. Judge the exact glossary entry against the strongest specific alternative; treat the chapter as evidence, not as an additional judgment target.
